I am auditing an effort estimate for SFCC-866: "Auto-Remove Cart Item When Moving to Wishlist if Item Already Exists in Wishlist". Current behaviour (SFCC OOTB) keeps the item in cart and shows an error when the shopper moves a cart item to wishlist and it's ALREADY in the wishlist. Desired: remove it from cart anyway, same as a normal move-to-wishlist.

Investigate READ-ONLY (do not modify any files) and report with absolute file paths + short exact code snippets for the load-bearing bits:

1. **Existing "move to wishlist" implementation.** Find it in BOTH:
   - `overrides/app/` (search `overrides/app/pages/cart/`, `overrides/app/components/`, especially `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`)
   - the base package `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/` and `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` generally
   Grep case-insensitively for: `wishlist`, `addItemToWishlist`, `moveToWishlist`, `Move to Wishlist`, `useWishlist`, `alreadyInWishlist`.

2. **The duplicate-check / error path specifically.** Find where the "item already in wishlist" condition is detected and where the error/toast message is raised. Quote the exact conditional and the toast/error call. Is the cart-removal skipped inside that branch? Show the control flow.

3. **Which files are already overridden vs still base-only.** For every file that would need changing, state clearly: does it ALREADY exist under `overrides/`, or would it need a fresh copy-first (copy from node_modules, JS→TS, fix imports)? This is the single most important output — it determines cost. List each file as either `ALREADY OVERRIDDEN: <path>` or `BASE ONLY, needs copy-first: <base path> -> <target overrides path>` and give the line count of the base file.

4. **In-flight SFCC-11 cart work.** `git status` shows many new `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` components. Run `git status --short` and `git diff --stat HEAD` and look for anything cart/wishlist related (e.g. zimmCartItemActions, wishlist auth drawer, zimmCartItem). Recent commits mention `wishlist-auth-drawer` and "persist pending intent when a guest creates a new account". Report what cart/wishlist components NOW exist that didn't before, with paths. Note there are unmerged (`UU`) conflict files — mention if any are cart/wishlist relevant.

5. **Wishlist hooks/utilities** anywhere under `overrides/app/hooks/` or base, and whether a wishlist list-contents lookup (to test membership) is already available client-side or would need a fetch.

6. Any `.docs/` content about wishlist or cart-item actions: check `.docs/prd/` and grep `.docs/` for wishlist. Also grep for `SFCC-272` and `SFCC-866` across the repo.

Be precise and evidence-led. Report file paths absolutely. Do not modify anything.

- Reading and analyzing file contents

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

content.text:
## Headline

SFCC-866 is **not a copy-first story** for the cart drawer surface. The entire move-to-wishlist flow has already been re-implemented in TypeScript under `overrides/` by the in-flight SFCC-11 work, and the "already in wishlist" branch is an explicit, documented, tested 3-line block. The behaviour change is **moving one `await onRemove()` call**. The only thing that could inflate the estimate is the base `/cart` page, which is still served OOTB and unoverridden — see §3b.

---

## 1. Move-to-wishlist implementation

### Overrides (the live drawer surface)

| File | Lines | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx` | 146 | **The branch point.** Owns `attemptMoveToWishlist` |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/usePendingWishlistItem.ts` | 155 | Guest pending-intent persistence + `WishlistMoveResult` type |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` | 817 | Owns `moveToWishlist`, `removeItem`, `alreadyInWishlistItemIds` state, inline message |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts` | 121 | `notifyAddedToWishlist` / `notifyAlreadyInWishlist` toasts |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` | 421 | Guest auth gate |
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx` | 122 | Single-trigger auth drawer |

The result contract (`usePendingWishlistItem.ts:16-19`):

```ts
export type WishlistMoveResult =
  | { status: 'success' }
  | { status: 'already-in-wishlist' }
  | { status: 'error'; error: unknown };
```

### Base package

- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx` — 1515 lines, `handleAddToWishlist` at line 422
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/partials/cart-secondary-button-group.jsx` — 160 lines, renders the "Add to Wishlist" button, passes `onAddToWishlistClick`
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-wish-list.js` — 42 lines, consumed directly by the override (not itself overridden, and does not need to be)

---

## 2. The duplicate-check and error path

### Where membership is detected — `cartDrawerContainer.tsx:698-706`

```ts
const moveToWishlist = async (productId: string): Promise<WishlistMoveResult> => {
  const isAlreadyInWishlist = wishlist?.customerProductListItems?.some(
    (item: { productId?: string }) => item.productId === productId,
  );
  if (isAlreadyInWishlist) {
    return { status: 'already-in-wishlist' };
  }
```

Note it **short-circuits before the mutation** — no network call is made.

### Where the cart removal is skipped — `zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx:111-123`

This is the exact load-bearing block for SFCC-866:

```ts
const attemptMoveToWishlist = useCallback(async () => {
  const result = await onMoveToWishlist();
  if (result.status === 'success') {
    await onRemove();
    notifyAddedToWishlist(productName);
  } else if (result.status === 'already-in-wishlist') {
    notifyAlreadyInWishlist();
    onAlreadyInWishlist?.();
  }
  // 'error': no AC or Figma copy exists for this branch — leave the item in the cart and emit
  // no message rather than invent feedback text
}, [onMoveToWishlist, onRemove, notifyAddedToWishlist, notifyAlreadyInWishlist, productName, onAlreadyInWishlist]);
```

**Control flow:** `onRemove()` lives *only* inside the `'success'` branch. The `'already-in-wishlist'` branch fires a warning toast plus a callback, and returns without touching the basket. That is precisely the OOTB behaviour SFCC-866 wants changed.

### The two pieces of user feedback on that branch

1. **Toast** — `useCartMessages.ts:45-47, 118`:
```ts
alreadyInWishlist: {
  id: 'use_cart_messages.already_in_wishlist',
  defaultMessage: 'An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist',
},
// ...
notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => emitCartMessage(intl.formatMessage(messages.alreadyInWishlist), 'warning'),
```

2. **Per-line inline message** — `cartDrawerContainer.tsx:327-338`, driven by the `onAlreadyInWishlist` callback into a `Set<string>` of item ids:
```ts
const isAlreadyInWishlist = Boolean(item.itemId) && alreadyInWishlistItemIds.has(item.itemId as string);
const message = isAtMaxQuantity
  ? { variant: 'warning' as const, text: t('cart.item.maxQuantityReached', '...') }
  : isAlreadyInWishlist
  ? { variant: 'warning' as const, text: t('cart.item.alreadyInWishlist', 'Item already exists in Wishlist') }
  : undefined;
```

This inline message is **Contentful-sourced** via `useUiCopy` (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:227`), so the copy key `cart.item.alreadyInWishlist` also exists in Contentful and would become dead if the branch is removed outright.

### Explicit design commitments that SFCC-866 reverses

Three places document "leave it in the cart" as intentional, all of which need editing so the codebase doesn't contradict itself:

- `zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx:39-41` — *"and again (at most once) if a wishlist move succeeds"*
- `useCartMessages.ts:63-64` — *"SFCC-272 AC6 — the item already exists in the shopper's wishlist; the caller leaves the cart line untouched"*
- `zimmCartItemActions/index.stories.tsx:92` — *"The item stays in the cart on this path (SFCC-272 AC6)"*

**SFCC-866 directly contradicts SFCC-272 AC6.** Worth flagging in the estimate as a spec-conflict item — AC6 should be formally superseded, not silently overwritten.

---

## 3. Override status of every file that would change

### 3a. Cart drawer surface (the in-scope work)

**Every single file is ALREADY OVERRIDDEN. Zero copy-first. Zero JS→TS. Zero import rewiring.**

```
ALREADY OVERRIDDEN: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx            (146 lines)  ← THE change
ALREADY OVERRIDDEN: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/index.test.tsx       (242 lines)  ← invert 2 assertions
ALREADY OVERRIDDEN: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/index.stories.tsx    (116 lines)  ← story + comment
ALREADY OVERRIDDEN: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts                                              (121 lines)  ← docblock; copy decision
ALREADY OVERRIDDEN: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx                                    (817 lines)  ← only if inline msg is dropped
ALREADY OVERRIDDEN: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.test.tsx                               (969 lines)  ← 2 tests
```

These are all **new files added on this branch** (`git diff --name-status origin/develop...HEAD` shows them as `A`) and are **committed clean** — nothing cart/wishlist related is dirty in the working tree.

The minimal code change is literally:

```ts
if (result.status === 'success') {
  await onRemove();
  notifyAddedToWishlist(productName);
} else if (result.status === 'already-in-wishlist') {
  await onRemove();            // ← added
  notifyAlreadyInWishlist();
  onAlreadyInWishlist?.();
}
```

…with an open product question on whether the toast/inline message stays (reworded, e.g. "already in your Wishlist — removed from bag") or goes. If the inline message goes, the `alreadyInWishlistItemIds` state machine (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:469-479`), the `onAlreadyInWishlist` prop chain, and its 2 container tests all become dead code to delete — that is the larger half of the work, and it is *deletion*, not construction.

### 3b. The base `/cart` page — the one real cost risk

`/cart` is **still served entirely from the base package, unoverridden**:

- `overrides/app/routes.tsx:20` — `const EXCLUDED_BASE_ROUTES = ['/category/:categoryId'];` — `/cart` is not excluded
- `overrides/app/routes.tsx` has no `/cart` entry at all (grep for `cart` returns nothing), so it falls through to `..._routes`
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx:105-106` supplies `path: '/cart'` → base `./pages/cart`

So the OOTB `handleAddToWishlist` at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:422-473` is live, with its own untouched skip-removal branch (`if (!isItemInWishlist) { ...add... } else { ...toast only... }` — and note it never calls remove on *either* branch).

```
BASE ONLY, needs copy-first: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx
                          -> /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/cart/index.tsx                                    (1515 lines)
BASE ONLY, needs copy-first: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/partials/cart-secondary-button-group.jsx
                          -> /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/cart/partials/cart-secondary-button-group.tsx     (160 lines)
```

**This is the estimate's swing factor.** `.docs/prd/cart.md` describes *both* surfaces — CAI-004 (mini-cart) and CAI-008 (cart page) — each with its own move-to-wishlist requirement. If SFCC-866 is scoped to the drawer only, it is a trivial ticket. If it must also cover `/cart`, you inherit a 1515-line JSX copy-first, which is an order of magnitude more expensive and almost certainly belongs in whatever ticket owns the cart page redesign rather than in SFCC-866. **Recommend confirming this scope boundary before sizing.**

---
